name: MCPJam Backend scenario redeems >30/h
description: PAGE · More than 30 scenario link redemptions this hour. Worst legit hour on record is 7.
Redeeming an anyone_with_link scenario was the entry route of the 2026-09-15 incident, and it moved two days before the money did.
npx convex data scenarios --prod --limit 3000 --order desc  — are the owners guests (isAnonymous)?
Then Railway edge logs for srcIp / clientUa on /api/web/scenarios/redeem.
A genuine launch of a shared scenario trips this too, and that is worth one message.
rationale: WHY THIS EXISTS: redeeming an anyone_with_link scenario is the entry route of vector 1 (visitor billed as the scenario owner). It went from 3-15 per DAY to 606 / 421 / 1,871 per day on 09-13/14/15 — the single loudest route-volume tell in the incident, and it moved two days before the money. Guest mints were NOT given a monitor: legit peaks (up to 1,125/h) overlap the abuse rate (1,036-1,138/h), so it is a dashboard tile only.

WHY THIS THRESHOLD: measured hourly redeems 08-25..09-12: max 7 in any hour. Abuse hours 64-399. 30 = 4x the worst legit hour; a real launch of a shared scenario will trip it and that is worth one message.

CONTEXT (2026-09-15 incident): $5,187 of MCPJam-paid spend in one UTC day. Every existing spend monitor fired correctly and posted to #mcpjam-alerts, but each is a single fixed threshold that notifies ONCE on crossing (Axiom threshold monitors only notify on state change; there is no re-notify while open). The daily page said '$107 is above $100' and then stayed silent while the day climbed to $5k, in a channel that also carries Sentry/PostHog/BE5 noise. Fan-out abuse (thousands of minted guests spending $1-3 each) moved the SPENDER COUNT 5-10x before the dollars did. This monitor set adds (a) a ladder of escalating spend tiers so a big day produces escalating messages, and (b) fan-out signals that lead the dollars.
SCOPE: only MCPJam's money — spendingPolicy=consume_mcpjam_limit AND modelSource=mcpjam. BYOK / record_only never cost us and are excluded (the older 'spend velocity' monitors sum everything).
